asset.name: USD Coin
issuerPowers: freeze (AUTH_REVOCABLE is set: the issuer can revoke the authorization of any balance, the vault's included)
flags not immutable (AUTH_IMMUTABLE is not set: the issuer can still set AUTH_REQUIRED or AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED; clawback then applies only to balances created afterwards)

verified.source: on-chain reading on https://horizon.stellar.org (accounts/<issuer>, assets?asset_code=USDC&asset_issuer=<issuer>): flags auth_required false, auth_revocable true, auth_immutable false, auth_clawback_enabled false; thresholds 2/2/2 over 4 signers; contract_id CCW67TS...MI75; the same id recomputed locally from the asset and the passphrase

unit.note: the vault itself is the adapter: it keeps its books in the L2 token's 6-decimal units and moves 10 stroops per unit; a deposit must be a multiple of 10 stroops, so nothing is rounded

fee.collection: accrued in the vault outside the backing; anyone calls sweep_fees() and the vault pays the recipient, which must exist and hold a USDC trustline
fee.networkFee: the depositor pays the deposit transaction; the relayer pays the release transaction (0.0166 XLM charged for a release with 5 signatures on a private network with the public network's per-transaction limits) and, for a queued release, its execution

finality.rule: Stellar closes a ledger by consensus and does not reorganise. A deposit is attested when its ledger is closed and at least 12 ledgers (about one minute) behind the signer's own node, that node is fresh, and every RPC the signer configures reports the same hash for that ledger. The deposit is read from the vault's state (its deposit chain), not from an event feed.
finality.reorg: There is no reorganisation to handle. A signer whose views of a closed ledger disagree, or whose node is stale, signs nothing (hold). Every mint still waits 12 hours on the L2, where the guardians cancel one whose deposit is not in the vault's chain.

deposit.recipientEncoding: BytesN<20>: the 20-byte L2 address (argument l2_recipient); no memo is used
deposit.function: deposit(from: Address, amount: i128 (stroops, a multiple of 10), l2_recipient: BytesN<20>)
deposit.approvalTarget: none: the depositor authorizes the vault call, which carries the asset transfer as a sub-invocation
steps: hold USDC on Stellar in the account or contract `from`
invoke deposit(from, amount, l2_recipient) on the vault, signed by `from`
after the ledger margin and the 12 hour mint delay the L2 token credits amount / 10 less 0.05% to l2_recipient
refusals: an amount that is not a multiple of 10 stroops, below minDeposit or above maxDeposit, or one that would pass the cap
a classic payment to the vault's address is not a deposit (a contract address cannot receive one); only the contract call is

release.l2Function: StellarBurnRouter.burnTo(uint64 amount, string stellarAddress) after approving the router; or token.burn(amount, commitment) directly
release.recipientEncoding: a Stellar G... account or C... contract address; the burn names its commitment, the low 20 bytes of keccak256(bytes32('BLOCH-XLM-RECIPIENT-v1') ‖ the 56-character address)
release.paysAsset: USDC on Stellar, the burned amount less 0.05%, in stroops (amount * 10)
notes: a G... recipient must already hold a USDC trustline; until it does the release stays unpaid and can be retried, it is not lost
every release waits release_delay (proposed 2 hours) in the vault's queue before anyone can execute it
a recipient whose authorization the issuer revoked cannot be paid until the issuer restores it
UNAUDITED. Nothing is deployed. Limits are the Ethereum bridge's launch values, proposed for this network; the owner confirms them before deployment.
limits are in custody units of 6 decimals (asset.unit); one unit is 10 stroops of the 7-decimal asset.

guardians: one guardian pauses the vault for 72 h by a signature that anyone relays (its secp256k1 key cannot sign a Stellar transaction). DIFFERENCE from the other networks (committee.guardianCancelQuorum): while the release delay is above 0, 2 of 3 guardians can also cancel a QUEUED release; a cancel pays no one, loses no burn (the burn id is free again) and 6 of 7 signers certify that burn again, once; that release cannot be cancelled. With delay 0 nothing queues and the guardians are pause-only in the strict sense. docs/STELLAR-BRIDGE.md section 4.

release delay (limits.releaseDelaySeconds with largeItemThreshold 0: every release queues): 7200 s is a PROPOSAL. The delay is a deployment parameter the owner decides; 0 gives the Ethereum launch behaviour. docs/STELLAR-BRIDGE.md section 5.
